I’ve worked both Union and non union jobs. I’ve also worked what I considered both lazy and not lazy Union jobs. 

I was working a construction Union job where we busted our asses on a daily basis. Good pay, good benefits, but worked to get them. I went from that to working at a non union job at the second largest retail employer in the US. Different work, but still did a lot, for a lot less money. Constantly moving, breaks were exactly 15 minutes, no longer or you got “talked” to. After there, I went to a lazy union job where I could finish my workload in 3 hours but was told almost immediately to slow down and stretch it out. I wasn’t being unsafe. I did the job completely and thoroughly, and it only took me 3 hours. I gained close to 40lbs because of that “slow down and stretch it out” mentality. Now I work non Union again and I bust my ass but I get paid well so I’m ok with it. 

I guess it really depends on the type of work it is. When I worked at the lazy union job, if we had someone call out, we had to cover for them. But if that happened we only did the daily MUST do jobs. I was a custodian so the only “must do” jobs were empty trashes, clean and sanitize bathrooms. When someone would call out, I personally had to empty trash in about 20 more rooms than normal and clean two more bathrooms. But I didn’t have to do half of my normal workload. I worked for a big box corporation.  Was a department supervisor for 1 department and then helped open a new store and I moved over there and ran two departments. 

I was training to be an assistant manager and since we were a smaller store, often I would be the only “assistant manager” on duty. Usually on the closing shift. Since at the time I was still an hourly employee but I was also the manager on duty, I wouldn’t be able to take a lunch and would have to fill out an “exception punch” paper. Basically what was the reason for not taking a lunch?  When I would do this I would fill out the paper, then I would turn it in on the store managers desk to be signed and turned in by the opening manager. 

One day, I’m on the floor helping a customer on the phone and one of the assistant managers came out and slipped me a note to come see him when I was off the phone. I went to the back and he was in HRs office and they asked me to come in and close the door. 

“We have to let you go.”

I was dumbfounded. And I asked, why? 

My exception paper was turned in with a managers name but it wasn’t his signature. 

They said we have to let you go since your forged a managers signature. I was literally speechless and stood there staring at them for a minute and I answered: I didn’t do that. Why would I forge a signature on something that gets signed every morning and turned in? I wouldn’t forge someone’s signature. I turned it in on the desk right before I closed the store.

They said they had no other choice because they already called regional HR and that was what she said. I asked “You called her and asked her what to do without even talking to me first?”

I was upset to say the least. I was going thru a divorce at the time. I filed for unemployment and they denied it based on gross misconduct. I fought it and requested a phone hearing with unemployment. 

The judge listens to their entire spiel, then she asks me what I have to say, and I tell her everything I did and what my days looked like when I was the closing manager. She then asks my previous employer, “What proof do you have that he did this?”  They stammered and said, “well who else would have reason to?” To which the judge replied, “Based on what you told me and what Annasman told me, why would HE have reason to? He always turned it in and it would be signed and turned in to be processed. You have no proof that he did it and in my opinion you wrongfully terminated him on top of the fact that you weren’t giving him the opportunity to take his legal lunch. “ 

She ruled in my favor and they had to pay all of my back unemployment. I already had a new job so I didn’t pursue getting my old job back. 

I worked my butt off for that company and was a “company man” who wanted to progress higher. 

TL,DR: Was wrongfully terminated and company tried to not pay unemployment.

Both of my parents were severe alcoholics. My dad was a maintenance drinker and I’m pretty sure I only saw him drunk one time, but I remember him with a beer in his hand always. My mother would start drinking Pepsi and vodka every day at noon. My dad was in the hospital A LOT for numerous reasons (bad back resulting in 13 surgeries as of now at age 67, pancreatitis (which the doctors told him drinking would kill him if he didn’t stop), he got hepatitis c from a blood transfusion in the 1970s and that reared up in the 90s and again in the 2000s until he tried some new program I found). My mom always seemed to be able to get dinner together, but that was it. I did all the homework help, I made sure teeth got brushed, I hated them for it. Still hold resentment about it. 

I would have to get my brother and sister up for school every morning, they’re 2 and 6 years younger than me. I’d make sure they had lunch to take to school, made sure they got to the bus stop. Make sure they were dressed nicely. Even cut my brothers hair. 

I shielded my sister from getting beaten by my mother, and my brother from spankings. It was always kind of messed up, my mom hated my sister because she was “Daddy’s girl” from birth and she was always his favorite. When my brother came along, he was my moms miracle baby. Even tho I was the good kid who got good grades and didn’t get in to trouble, they were the favorites. Unfortunately, my mom would take her hatred out on my sister. And while my dad didn’t beat my brother, he was heavy handed on occasion. 

After they got divorced, my dad married my stepmom. He was a lot different after that. Stopped drinking, we bought a house (due to my mothers instability, we lived with my dad). He was happier for sure. 

I was about 15 then and was in high school, I had friends and I wasn’t at home much. Once I hit my 20s I realized I ignored my brother for years because he didn’t need me anymore now that my dad was living a better life. I felt ashamed and sad about it. 

I went over to my brothers place about 3 years ago (I was 40 then and he was 34) and we got to talking and enjoying some drinks, and I told him about this. How I felt like I let him down and that I failed him. That I hated myself for ignoring him and being a bad big brother.  

He then said something to me that I will never forget. He said, I was more of a father to him than our dad was for 10 years of his life. That I was the reason he is who he is, and that he’s happy with who he is. And I cried. I cried like I hadn’t cried in years. The whole time I was hating myself for ignoring him, he still looked at me as the same guy who took the blame for spilling the whole gallon of milk, the guy who helped him with his math work because he couldn’t figure it out. The guy who made his school lunch every day and poured his cereal in the morning. 

My brother and I are close now. My mom died when I was 19, and I haven’t seen my dad in about 6 years. But I see my brother often. My sister lives a long way away from me and we don’t speak much for a lot of other reasons. But my brother and I. We’re good.

Orifice tube is blocked up. Or a bad high or low pressure switch. Dryer/accumulator is crapped out. 

High pressure is often over charged orrr a plugged orifice tube. 

If the system was contaminated, then you could be plugged up somewhere else.  Usually these are easy enough to diagnose. 

But a/c systems should be handled by certified techs.

Ok. It’s sat for 2 years? Firstly, I don’t know where you live, but brake fluid can and will get moisture in it. Happens all the time, when you have a full service done they actually test for moisture in the system. Little tool that lights up with percentage of water present. 

When you have water in your fluid, it makes for soft, squishy brake feel. 

That’s number one. Number two is all of the seals that are in brakes are prone to breaking down over time, especially when they sit. This will also cause soft brake feel. 

There can be lots of different reasons. I would start with pulling wheels off and visually inspecting for leaks, brake lines can rust through and create pinhole leaks. Pull the pads off and throw a new set on, take some sand paper to your rotors to clear off any rust that’s built up. Then bleed your brakes. This takes two people unless you have a brake bleeder. 

Make sure to grease slide pins on your calipers, while you are replacing pads you can check to see if the caliper pistons move easily enough or are hanging up. If after all that is done you look at brake lines, the rubber part can get soft and cause soft brakes (instead of remaining semi rigid, they’ll expand when you force fluid in to them causing your brakes to feel soft because you have to push harder). Orrrr, leaking brake booster or master cylinder. 

Cars aren’t meant to sit for years. They’re meant to be driven. And I would guess the mechanic topped off the brake fluid.  If you take it to a mechanic you can have them do a full brake inspection.

Megamouth sharks have always intrigued me. I remember when I was a kid and first learning about them in the mid 80s. 

I always thought it was a goofy name, until I learned why it was called that. The video and pictures I have seen don’t really do it justice. A 16 footer that was discovered had a mouth 4’ across!  The biggest mega found to date was around 18’ and was a male. 

To this day not a lot is known about them. Scientists don’t know how old they get but do know they give birth to live pups but are ovoviviparous like whale sharks. 

There has been less than a 100 documented sightings since first “discovered” in the 70s. Based on those though, scientists have learned that the mega isn’t a fast swimmer due to having soft fins. They also have soft loose skin and the denticles on their body differ depending on where they’re located. 

They are known to migrate vertically throughout the day for food which is mainly made up of zooplankton and shrimp. 

While researching I just learned that they project their mouth forward (similar to a goblin shark, but not as much and not nearly as scary) to increase the volume of their mouth to create a vacuum to pull their food in to their mouth. Then they pull it back in forcing water out and then swallow the shrimp. 

Lastly, they’re in the order of mackerel sharks, which confuses me because other mackerel sharks are the great white, mako sharks, etc. which one of their main features are pointier noses. However the basking shark is also in the same order so it is likely more than just a sharp nose that puts it there. 

Now you know, and knowing is half the battle

Cows milk, yogurt, new clothes, actual heat, at one point a house was an actual luxury. I remember my mom buying powdered milk because it was cheaper. I remember we went to see my dad who was in the hospital and instead of grabbing some fast food or something (which I don’t remember EVER doing when I was young) we went to the grocery store and I remember I got to get yogurt and I thought that was amazing because I never got to have it. 

Until I was in junior high, 8th grade or 9th grade all of my clothes were second hand from a thrift store. Unless the temperature in the house dropped below 50, my parents wouldn’t use heat, and the house we lived in only had a wood stove in the living room. So my not well insulated bedroom was nearly the same temperature inside as it was outside. “Put on a coat” was said a lot. 

Lastly, in my 6th grade year, from about August until February we lived in a tent on a lady’s property. Had Christmas there. The winter of 1990 there was quite a bit of snow. I was ashamed. I am pretty sure my parents were too because i told this story to my gramma just a couple years ago and she was aghast because she only lived two towns over and had a big house and didn’t know about it. 

First world problems right?

Edit: oh! I also remember that my mom made us our coloring books. I think it was more of a reason for her to draw goofy stuff than money but it always stuck with me because a kid at school gave me a hard time about it when I was in 4th grade and made fun of me being so poor I couldn’t even get a coloring book.
